ap_computer_science_a-m02.stem: What is printed as a result of executing the code segment?

options.why: Believes the cast in (double) (a / b) makes the division exact.
a / b is integer division giving 7, widened to 7.0; (double) a / b is exact: 7.25; casting the result of a / b gives 7.0 again. Tracing the code gives 7.0 7.25 7.0.
Reads the first division as a remainder.
Believes the cast to double is applied after the integer division, so e is the truncated value.

ap_computer_science_a-m04.stem: Which of the following is the weakest precondition (the least restrictive condition) that guarantees the method slice will not throw an exception?

options.text: start is at least 0, len is at least 0, and start + len is at most s.length().
options.why: substring needs 0 <= start and start + len <= s.length(), and a negative len makes the end index smaller than start.

options.text: len is at most s.length() and start is any int value.
options.why: This does not prevent start + len from passing the end, as slice("hello", 3, 4) shows.

options.text: start is at least 0, and len is greater than 0 and at most s.length().
options.why: This is stronger than needed and also incomplete: it does not stop start + len from exceeding s.length().

options.text: start + len is less than s.length() and neither start nor len is negative.
options.why: This is stronger than needed (start + len may equal s.length()), although it does exclude negative values of start and len.

blueprint.subject: ap_computer_science_a
blueprint.concept: a precondition combines every constraint a call needs
student_thinking: read the code and decide which statement about it is true
compare the result with each option and rule out the named misconceptions

key_conditions.condition: each claim was checked by compiling or running the code with the JDK

misconceptions.description: This does not prevent start + len from passing the end, as slice("hello", 3, 4) shows.
This is stronger than needed and also incomplete: it does not stop start + len from exceeding s.length().
This is stronger than needed (start + len may equal s.length()), although it does exclude negative values of start and len.

verification.independent_path: java runs on valid and invalid start and length values
